thread:
emily: Heads-up — metering adapter v2 flagged a contract edge case in staging, blocking the pricing rollout. Anyone owning gateway->billing path?
rahul: I'm infra but not the adapter owner. Can you paste the exact error/log? :eyes:
emily: here's the log snippet from staging:```
ERROR: billing_contract_match: missing quota_config for plan_id=1023
  at Adapter.validate (adapter.py:214)
  at MeteringRouter.route (router.py:89)
```
sarah: billing here — that missing quota_config is our legacy-plan-carryover issue. plan_id 1023 wasn't mapped during the packaging->pricing migration. @mike do we still expect 1023 to exist for launched customers?
mike: Product confirms plan 1023 is active for a small set of legacy/EA customers. We can't drop it. This is P1 for the rollout. We need a short-term guard and a migration.
jen: Legal/Contracts: don't silently remap contract IDs. If you change mappings add an audit entry and notify affected customers.
rahul: Two options: 1) quick migration script to populate quota_config for 1023, 2) fallback in adapter to treat missing quota as "preserve-old". Migration is preferred. Who owns the script?
emily: alex from eng-ml did some of the packaging migrations earlier, tagging him now. @alex can you pick this up?
alex: I can own the migration script and CR. ETA ~3h to get a tested script + staging run. Will open a PR and mark for expedited review.
emily: thanks. Please include: (a) migration idempotent SQL/DB update, (b) a revert plan, (c) a test case that replicates the staging failure. Also add a short runbook step for on-call.
rahul: I'll prep a quick canary flow in infra so we can limit to 10% traffic after migration.
mike: Once PR is up, I'll coordinate comms to the affected customers. Need to avoid surprises.
jen: Add a line in the contract audit sheet with migration ticket id before deploy.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: canary rollout pending manual approval.
emily: OK — plan: alex builds PR (ETA 3h), rahul preps canary, emily + mike confirm comms, jen updates audit. If anyone objects to migration approach speak up now. Otherwise we proceed. :thumbsup:
